title: Decode One Instruction
blurb: Target: Windows x86-64. Decode the raw byte sequence 0F B6 41 08 into its x86-64 assembly instruction and explain what it does. --- Answer: movzx eax, byte ptr [rcx+8]. Explanation: 1) 0F B6 is the two-byte opcode for movzx r32, r/m8 -- moves a byte operand into a 32-bit register with zero-extension, clearing the upper 24 bits (unlike movsx, which sign-extends). 2) ModRM byte 41 = 01 000 001: mod=01 selects a disp8 memory operand, reg=000 selects eax as the destination, rm=001 selects rcx as the base register; the trailing disp8 byte 08 gives effective address [rcx+8]. 3) On the Windows x64 calling convention, rcx holds the first integer/pointer argument, so this reads a single byte field at offset 8 of the struct rcx points to and zero-extends it into eax -- a common pattern for loading a bool or uint8_t struct member.
